content.text:
I couldn't run the cleanup. All 7 `expire_snapshots` calls came back with "tool call limit reached; not run", so nothing was expired and every table still has its full snapshot history.

Before trying, I listed every table and checked its history:

| Table | Snapshots | Would be expired |
|---|---|---|
| db.customers | 3 | 2 |
| db.customers_pii | 2 | 1 |
| db.events | 6 | 5 |
| db.orders | 8 | 7 |
| db.orders_staging | 2 | 1 |
| prod.customers | 1 | 0 (nothing to do) |
| prod.orders | 3 | 2 |

That's 18 old snapshots across 6 tables. Every snapshot is an append, so I saw nothing like a bad overwrite or delete that you might want to roll back first. Still, expiring down to 1 snapshot means you can no longer time-travel or roll back to anything older than the current state. That matters most for `prod.orders`, which would lose its Jul 27 and Oct 5 versions.

Once the tool limit resets, I can rerun the same calls (`older_than` = now, `retain_last` = 1) if you want. Expiring snapshots doesn't always delete the data files right away. If the storage bill doesn't drop, running `remove_orphan_files` afterwards would clear out files that no snapshot uses anymore.
